name: Silk Milk Cleanser
short: A no-foam milk cleanser that lifts the day off without stripping the skin.
description: Silk Milk is a soft, non-foaming cleanser built for mornings and for taking off a light layer of makeup. Massaged onto dry skin it slips; rinsed off, it leaves the face pliant rather than squeaky. It works well as the second cleanse after a balm.
details: Squalane and glycerin keep the barrier comfortable

name: Oat & Kaolin Renewing Cleanser
short: Fine white clay and colloidal oatmeal in a cream that gently resurfaces.
description: A cream cleanser holding a whisper of kaolin and colloidal oatmeal, made for skin that gets congested along the jaw and nose. It emulsifies into a thin milk as you work it, so the clay never drags across the surface. Skin reads smoother after a week of nightly use.
details: Colloidal oatmeal calms the look of redness
Low-foam cream that turns to milk

name: Charcoal Clarifying Gel Cleanser
short: A clear gel with activated charcoal and zinc for oily, congested skin.
description: A transparent gel that foams lightly and rinses clean, with activated charcoal and zinc PCA to keep shine down through the day. It is written for skin that goes grey by lunchtime and for anyone who trains in the evening. Follow with a hydrating toner while the skin is damp.

name: Melt Cleansing Balm
short: A solid balm that turns to oil and rinses away without a film.
description: Melt is a firm, scoopable balm that becomes oil against warm skin and takes waterproof mascara with it. Emulsified with water it rinses to a clear finish, with no greasy film left on the mirror. It is step one of a double cleanse, always.
details: Rice bran and sunflower seed oils
Scoop and warm between the fingertips

name: Salicylic 2 Clarifying Cleanser
short: A two per cent salicylic wash for breakouts along the chin and forehead.
description: A gentle cleansing gel buffered with 2 per cent salicylic acid and glycerin, so it helps clear the look of breakouts without leaving the skin flaking. Leave it on for thirty seconds before rinsing and it works considerably better. Introduce it on alternate evenings and build from there.
details: 2 per cent salicylic acid, a BHA
Helps clear the look of breakouts

name: Amino Foam Cleanser
short: Amino-acid surfactants, a soft foam, and a rinse that feels like nothing.
description: A cleansing foam built on amino-acid surfactants that lifts oil and leaves no slick behind. The lather is airy rather than aggressive, and the dispensed dollop is soft enough to work near the eyes. A good first cleanser for people who dislike first cleansers.

name: Rose Micellar Water
short: Micelles, rose water and panthenol for a no-rinse cleanse on light days.
description: Micelles small enough to pick up oil and dust, suspended in a rose and panthenol base that leaves skin comfortable rather than sticky. Pour it over a flat pad and press rather than scrub, and the eyes stay calm. Keep it for travel and for nights when a sink is too much to ask.

name: Rice Enzyme Powder Cleanser
short: A dry powder with rice enzymes that turns to milk in wet hands.
description: A weightless powder that activates with water into a soft milk, polishing dull skin with rice enzymes and finely milled rice bran. Nothing is mixed in advance, so every dose is fresh and the formula needs no heavy preservative. Use it three or four mornings a week in place of a gel.
details: Rice enzymes and milled rice bran

name: Centella Soothing Toner
short: A weightless watery toner steeped in centella asiatica.
description: Centella asiatica leaf extract in a thin, watery toner that settles flushed skin over two passes of the hands. It layers under everything without pilling, which is the entire argument for a toner. Keep it in the fridge through summer if you like the shock of it.

name: First Dew Essence
short: Polyglutamic acid in a slim, watery essence that holds water on the skin.
description: A hydrating essence with polyglutamic acid and a little rice ferment, pressed into damp skin to hold the water your cleanser just took away. It slips in under serum and helps the next layer travel further. Light enough for the most humid month of the year.
details: Rice ferment adds a soft glow

name: Niacinamide Refining Toner
short: Five per cent niacinamide in a toner for visible pores and uneven tone.
description: A watery toner with 5 per cent niacinamide and zinc, aimed at the look of enlarged pores along the cheeks and an uneven tone across the nose. It absorbs in seconds and never turns tacky under sunscreen. Use it morning and night on skin that is still damp from the cleanser.
details: 5 per cent niacinamide with zinc PCA
Sharpens the look of pores and tone

name: Rice Ferment Glow Toner
short: Double-fermented rice water for skin that looks tired rather than clear.
description: Double-fermented rice water, lightly filtered, with a touch of glycerin; a toner for skin that reads dull after a difficult week. It carries a faint scent of the grain itself and nothing added on top. Press it in before your serum and the whole face looks brighter by lunchtime.
details: No added fragrance, smells of grain

name: AHA 8 Resurfacing Toner
short: Glycolic and lactic acid at 8 per cent for a weekly texture reset.
description: A buffered blend of glycolic and lactic acid that smooths rough texture and lifts dull surface cells across a week of nights. It stings briefly on freshly shaved skin, so avoid the jaw for the first two uses. A cotton pad or clean fingertips both do the job equally well.
details: 8 per cent AHA, glycolic and lactic
Use at night, two or three times weekly
Patch test and wear SPF next morning
Avoid the same night as retinoids

name: Mugwort Calming Mist
short: A fine mist of mugwort and green tea for hot, reactive skin.
description: Mugwort extract and green tea in a mist fine enough to pass over makeup at three in the afternoon. It cools the look of flush and takes the tightness out of an air-conditioned room. Keep one on the desk and one in the bag, and refill both from the large bottle.

name: Green Tea Essence Lotion
short: A milky lotion brewed with green tea for antioxidant morning care.
description: A light milky lotion made with cold-brewed green tea and a little squalane, designed as an antioxidant first step for city skin. It drinks in quickly and leaves a faint satin rather than shine. Good under sunscreen for the days a serum feels like too many steps.
details: Cold-brewed green tea, rich in polyphenols

name: Vitamin C 15 Brightening Serum
short: Ethyl ascorbic acid at 15 per cent, stable in the bottle and never sticky.
description: A water-light serum using 15 per cent ethyl ascorbic acid, the derivative that stays clear in the bottle and does not turn your pillowcase orange. Paired with ferulic acid and vitamin E, it fades the look of dark marks slowly and evenly over a season. Wear it in the morning, under sunscreen.
details: Stabilised with ferulic acid and vitamin E
Fades the look of post-sun marks
Stays clear six months after opening

specs.v: Ethyl ascorbic acid 15 per cent, ferulic acid

name: Ascorbyl Phosphate 10 Serum
short: Sodium ascorbyl phosphate for skin that finds vitamin C irritating.
description: A gentler brightening serum built on sodium ascorbyl phosphate, which converts slowly on the skin and does not sting a compromised barrier. It suits reactive complexions, and it sits comfortably alongside niacinamide. Give it eight weeks before deciding whether it is working.

name: Niacinamide 10 Zinc Serum
short: Ten per cent niacinamide with zinc, reformulated so it never pills.
description: Ten per cent niacinamide with 1 per cent zinc PCA in a gel serum reworked with less film-former, so it no longer rolls off under sunscreen. It calms shine, softens the look of pores and evens tone across a season of use. The staple of the range for blemish-prone skin.
details: 10 per cent niacinamide, 1 per cent zinc PCA
Reduces the look of shine and pores

name: Three Weight Hyaluronic Serum
short: Three molecular weights of hyaluronic acid for a plumper-looking face.
description: High, mid and low molecular weight hyaluronic acid in one serum, so hydration sits on the surface and draws deeper as it dries. Apply it to damp skin and seal with a cream inside the same minute. It is the least glamorous bottle in the range and the one people quietly repurchase.
details: High, mid and low molecular weight HA
Plumps the look of fine lines
Gel-light, no tack after sixty seconds

name: Retinaldehyde 0.05 Night Serum
short: Retinaldehyde, one step from the prescription form, in a slow-release cream.
description: Retinaldehyde at 0.05 per cent works faster than retinol and irritates less than you would expect, because it is suspended in an oat-lipid cream that releases it gradually. Begin with two nights a week and build as tolerance allows. The bottle is opaque for a reason; keep it that way.
details: Encapsulated in an oat lipid cream
Smooths texture and softens the look of lines

name: Bakuchiol Comfort Serum
short: A plant-derived smoothing serum for skin that cannot hold a retinoid.
description: A gentle smoothing serum built on 1 per cent bakuchiol and squalane, for those who go red at the mention of retinol. It is a dry oil that sinks in overnight and leaves no mark on the pillow. Use it nightly; it does not sensitise skin to the sun the way stronger actives can.

name: Azelaic Fluid 10
short: A weightless azelaic acid fluid for marks, flush and blocked pores.
description: Azelaic acid at 10 per cent in a thin fluid that does not pill under makeup, made for the marks left behind and the persistent redness around the nose. It reads slightly powdery on application before settling, which is normal for this active at this strength. Give it six honest weeks.
details: Fades the look of post-blemish marks

name: Peptide Complex Firm Serum
short: Four signal peptides in a satin serum for the look of firmness.
description: A firming serum combining a four-peptide complex with a little panthenol, formulated at a pH that keeps everything working together rather than fighting. It gives an immediate satin finish and, after a month, a bounce you can feel with a fingertip. Press it into the jaw and down the neck.

name: Centella Repair Serum
short: A honey-toned centella serum for skin recovering from over-exfoliation.
description: A concentrated centella asiatica serum with madecassoside and a slip of glycerin, written for the shiny, tight look of a barrier you have worked too hard. It stings almost never, which is how you know it is on your side. Layer it under anything, including a retinoid on the nights you keep going.
details: Rebuilds the look of a compromised barrier

name: Panthenol Comfort Drops
short: Pro-vitamin B5 drops for skin that feels thin and angry in winter.
description: High-dose panthenol with ectoin and glycerin in a light drop that takes the bite out of cold air and hot showers alike. It is the serum to pair with a strong active rather than to use instead of one. Two drops pressed over the cheeks before cream is genuinely enough.

name: Turmeric Brightening Serum
short: A soft gold serum with turmeric and rice bran for dull, uneven tone.
description: Turmeric root extract with rice bran and vitamin E in a milky serum that leaves a faint warm glow rather than a yellow stain. It suits skin that looks flat in the middle of winter and takes a while to show anything. Shake before each use, as the pigment likes to settle.
details: Warm gold tint that does not stain on damp skin

name: Glycolic 7 Texture Serum
short: A low-strength glycolic serum for nightly smoothing short of a peel.
description: Seven per cent glycolic acid buffered with arginine for a slow nightly resurfacing that stops short of a treatment. It makes the skin look like skin again after a year of congestion and closed texture. Start on two nights a week, and skip it on the nights you use retinaldehyde.
details: 7 per cent glycolic acid, arginine buffered
Refines the look of texture and dullness

name: Ceramide Barrier Cream
short: Three ceramides and cholesterol in a cream that fixes the tightness.
description: A rich but non-greasy cream with ceramides NP, AP and EOP plus cholesterol and fatty acids in ratios the skin recognises. It is what we reach for after a retinoid, after a long flight, and after anything else the skin has been through. Deeply comfortable and never heavy on the face.
details: Ceramides NP, AP and EOP with cholesterol
Ratios matched to the skin barrier

name: Weightless Day Gel
short: A water-gel moisturiser for skin that refuses cream in July.
description: A hydrating gel with hyaluronic acid, green tea and a whisper of squalane that cools on contact and then disappears. Under sunscreen it behaves, and over it nothing moves. Written for oily, humid-climate skin that still needs water more than oil.

name: Shea & Marula Night Cream
short: A dense, slow-absorbing night cream that holds the whole routine in.
description: Shea butter, marula oil and a little rice bran in a cream thick enough to seal a routine and good enough to sleep on. It melts at skin temperature instead of sitting on the surface until morning. Use it on the hands in winter as well as on the face.
details: Softens the look of dehydration lines
Warm natural scent, no fragrance added

specs.v: Shea butter, marula oil, vitamin E

name: Centella Water Cream
short: A bouncy gel-cream with centella for skin that flushes easily.
description: A light gel-cream built on centella asiatica and panthenol that settles redness and hydrates without any weight at all. It reads dewy for a minute and then turns into skin. A good single moisturiser for anyone who will not be doing a serum.

name: Oat Calming Balm
short: A concentrated balm for cheeks, lips and any patch that will not settle.
description: Colloidal oatmeal, squalane and shea pressed into a small, dense balm you warm between two fingers and press onto the places that hurt. It is not a face cream; it is a spot treatment for dryness. Good on windburn and on the raw edges of the nose in cold months.
details: Warm and press onto dry patches
Use on cheeks, lips and nose edges

name: Green Tea Balancing Lotion
short: A runny lotion for oily skin that still needs hydrating.
description: A lotion thin as water with green tea, zinc PCA and niacinamide, made to hydrate oily skin without adding to it. It layers three times in the height of summer and never pills. The bottle is large because you will use more of it than you expect.
details: Green tea, zinc PCA and niacinamide
Fluid lotion that absorbs in seconds

name: Sea Buckthorn Day Cream
short: Bright from sea buckthorn, mildly tart, for winter dullness.
description: Sea buckthorn oil and carrot seed extract give this cream a genuine orange tone and a dense hit of antioxidants for skin that goes grey by February. It tints very faintly on application and then evens out into nothing. Pair it with a sunscreen by the middle of the day.
details: Sea buckthorn with carrot seed oil
Faint warm tint that settles clear

name: Neroli Comfort Cream
short: A soft cream scented only with neroli water, for skin that likes a ritual.
description: A medium-weight cream with squalane, glycerin and a small amount of genuine neroli distillate; the only fragranced moisturiser in the range, and lightly at that. It is written for skin that finds unscented boring and can still tolerate a real floral. Use it morning or night.
details: Medium weight with a satin finish

name: Barrier Repair Body Lotion
short: Ceramides for the arms and legs, in a bottle worth the size.
description: A large, unscented body lotion with ceramides, glycerin and squalane for skin that goes ashy within an hour of the shower. It absorbs fast enough to dress immediately and leaves only a faint satin at the elbows. Face and body share the same barrier, after all.
details: Ceramides and glycerin for body skin

name: Invisible Sun Fluid SPF 50
short: A thin, weightless fluid that disappears on every depth of skin.
description: A filter fluid that shakes like water and finishes with no white cast at all, on deep tones as readily as light ones. It is the sunscreen people actually reapply, because it feels like nothing on the face. Two finger widths of it cover the face and neck honestly.
details: No cast on deep skin tones
Fluid texture, absorbs within a minute

name: Mineral Sunscreen SPF 30
short: Zinc oxide, unfragranced, for skin that reacts to chemical filters.
description: A non-nano zinc mineral sunscreen for reactive, recently over-exfoliated or filter-sensitive skin. It warms in and fades to a soft satin; on very deep tones it can read slightly ashy, so buff it in with damp fingertips. Gentle enough to use right up to the lash line.

name: Tinted Day Fluid SPF 40
short: A skin-tone fluid with SPF 40 that covers as much as it protects.
description: A lightweight tinted fluid with SPF 40 in five adaptable shades, for the days you want one product to be the whole face. It evens redness and old sun marks and photographs like skin rather than makeup. Blend it with a fingertip, not a brush, and it will not go patchy.
details: Not a substitute for midday reapplication

name: Sun Stick SPF 50
short: A solid SPF stick for honest touch-ups over makeup.
description: A twist-up stick of SPF 50 with squalane and vitamin E that glides over foundation without moving it, which is the only realistic way to reapply at three in the afternoon. It fits in a coat pocket and will not leak inside a bag. Drag it across the cheekbones, the nose and the ears.
details: Solid twist-up, no liquid for hand luggage

name: After Sun Recovery Gel
short: A cool aloe and panthenol gel for skin that spent the day outside.
description: Aloe, panthenol and centella in a gel that goes cold-ish on contact and takes the heat out of over-exposed skin. Keep it in the fridge and use it on the shoulders as readily as the face. It is not a sunscreen and does not prevent anything on its own.
details: Cools the feel of over-exposed skin

name: Kaolin & Dead Sea Clay Masque
short: A creamy clay masque that draws out congestion and never cracks.
description: White kaolin and dead sea salt in a creamy masque that stays workable for ten minutes instead of drying into a crust. It pulls the oil out of the T-zone and leaves the cheeks alone entirely. Rinse it away with a warm cloth rather than scrubbing at it.
details: Kaolin clay with dead sea salt

name: Bentonite & Charcoal Purifying Masque
short: The deep-clearing one, for the week after too much sunscreen.
description: A strong bentonite and charcoal masque that shrinks slightly as it dries and lifts the grey out of a congested nose. It is not for dry or sensitive skin, and it is not a weekly habit for most people. Rinse before it fully sets and follow with a hydrating toner on damp skin.
details: Once every seven to ten days

name: Overnight Rice Sleeping Mask
short: A bouncy overnight mask with rice ferment that shows by morning.
description: A sleeping mask with rice ferment, squalane and a light film that holds hydration against the pillow all night. You wake with skin that looks rested rather than shiny. A pea-sized amount is genuinely enough for the whole face, and more will only transfer to the sheet.
details: Rice ferment and squalane overnight seal

name: Jojoba Bead Polishing Scrub
short: Soft jojoba beads, no plastic, for a one-minute surface polish.
description: Round jojoba ester beads in a cream base give a real but gentle polish, with nothing angular enough to scratch. Use it before a mask or before a trip, not once a week out of habit. The nose and the forehead are the whole job on most faces.
details: One minute, once weekly at most

name: Lactic 5 Overnight Peel
short: A low-strength lactic peel you sleep in, for dry rough texture.
description: Five per cent lactic acid at a gentle pH, in a leave-on peel you apply two nights a week and do not rinse. Lactic hydrates while it exfoliates, which is why it suits dry skin that finds glycolic too sharp. The bottle is opaque because lactic does not enjoy light.
details: Hydrating AHA, kind to dry skin
Introduce slowly and use SPF each morning
Do not combine with retinaldehyde the same night

name: Peptide Eye Cream
short: A fine peptide cream for the crepey look under the eyes.
description: A light eye cream with peptides, squalane and caffeine that smooths the crepe under the eyes enough to make concealer behave properly. It is unscented and safe right on the lash line. One grain-of-rice amount per eye, tapped in with the ring finger.

name: Caffeine De-Puff Fluid
short: A cool fluid with caffeine and rice peptide for morning puffiness.
description: A watery fluid with 5 per cent caffeine, a rice peptide and a little centella that moves the morning puffiness out from under the eyes. Store it cool and apply with a fingertip, tapping outward toward the temple. It does very little for pigment, which is worth saying out loud.
details: 5 per cent caffeine with rice peptide
Reduces the look of morning puffiness

specs.v: Caffeine 5 per cent, rice peptide, centella

name: Retinal Eye Cream 0.03
short: The low-strength retinaldehyde your lash line can tolerate.
description: Retinaldehyde at 0.03 per cent in a rich, small-gauge eye cream for the fine lines at the outer corner. It is deliberately weaker than the face serum for precisely this reason. Build up to every other night, and stop for a week if the lid goes flaky.
details: For fine lines at the outer corner

name: Hydrogel Eye Patches
short: Six pairs of hydrogel patches soaked in centella for one long evening.
description: Thin hydrogel patches soaked in centella, panthenol and rice ferment that stay put for twenty minutes and leave the under-eye looking less hollow. Reach for them before an event or after a long flight. The foil seal matters more than the essence inside it, so check it.
details: Hydrogel soaks in rather than drying out
Twelve patches in six foil pairs
Twenty minutes, then press in the rest

name: Squalane & Rosehip Facial Oil
short: Two oils and nothing else, for skin that needs sealing at night.
description: Refined rosehip and olive-derived squalane in a dry oil that sinks within a minute and leaves no shine on the pillow. Two oils are considerably easier to get right than twelve. Press it in as the final step over skin that is still damp from the serum.
details: Dry oil that absorbs in a minute
Rich in vitamin E and linoleic acid

name: Marula & Camellia Night Oil
short: A richer pressing of marula and camellia for cold months.
description: Marula and camellia oils with a trace of sea buckthorn; a warmer, more emollient pressing for winter and for mature skin that has gone thirsty. It leaves a visible soft glow at ten at night and none by breakfast. Three drops into warm hands, then press.
details: Marula, camellia and a trace of sea buckthorn
More emollient than the Squalane blend
Three drops is a full face

name: Jojoba Balance Oil
short: Cold-pressed jojoba, the oil closest to what your own skin makes.
description: Jojoba is a liquid wax that skin reads as its own, which is why this single-oil serum tends to calm oily skin instead of adding to it. It is light enough to wear in the morning under sunscreen. Massage one drop into the jawline and down the neck before it is fully dry.

name: Shea Lip Mask
short: A thick, plain lip mask for overnight repair of cracked lips.
description: Shea butter, castor seed oil and a beeswax-free base pressed into a small pot you spoon onto the lips before bed. It tastes of nothing at all, which is deliberate. It is equally good on cuticles and on the edges of the nose during cold months.
details: Shea butter with castor seed oil
Plain, with no flavour or fragrance
Small pot with a fitted lid

name: Peptide Lip Butter
short: A soft, non-plumping peptide butter that makes lips look full by being healthy.
description: A creamy lip treatment with a smoothing peptide complex and murumuru butter that softens the vertical lines over time simply by keeping the surface fully hydrated. It wears under and over lipstick without sliding. Nothing tingles, because tingling has never been a result.

name: Double Cleanse Duo
short: The balm and the foam together, in the two sizes you actually travel with.
description: Melt Cleansing Balm in a 30 ml tin and the Amino Foam in a 60 ml tube, sized for a cabin bag and for a gym kit. Together they take long-wear makeup off properly in about ninety seconds. It is also the cheapest way to try the range before committing to full bottles.
details: 30 ml balm tin with 60 ml foam tube
A full double cleanse in ninety seconds

name: Lactic Body Smoothing Lotion
short: A runny lactic acid lotion for rough bumps on the arms and thighs.
description: A light body lotion with 10 per cent lactic acid and urea, formulated for the small rough bumps on the back of the upper arms and for thighs that go gritty after shaving. It absorbs in under a minute and does not leave a film on bedding. Wear sunscreen on exposed areas, as with any acid.
details: 10 per cent lactic acid with urea
For keratosis-style roughness on arms and legs
Fast absorbing, no residue on clothing
Use nightly, then every other day
SPF on exposed skin while using it

name: Neck and Chest Peptide Cream
short: A thicker cream for the two places everyone forgets until later.
description: A firming cream with a peptide complex, squalane and a little niacinamide, deliberately heavier than a face cream so it stays on the neck long enough to matter. It is made for horizontal lines at the throat and the sun-damaged plane of the chest. Massage upward, and follow with SPF in the morning.
details: Heavier base so it stays on the neck
Smooths the look of horizontal throat lines

name: Back and Chest Clarifying Wash
short: A salicylic body wash for the breakouts that sit under a shirt.
description: A foaming body wash with 2 per cent salicylic acid and zinc, made for the back, chest and shoulders where sweat and sunscreen block the pores. Leave the lather on for a minute before rinsing, and use a long-handled brush if the reach is the problem. It will not help hormonal breakouts below the jaw, which are a different matter.
details: 2 per cent salicylic acid body wash
Zinc PCA for the look of shine
Hold the lather for sixty seconds
Use on back, chest and shoulders only

specs.v: Salicylic acid 2 per cent, zinc PCA

name: Sun Powder SPF 50
short: A tinted powder that tops up your sunscreen over makeup at noon.
description: A pressed mineral powder with SPF 50 and zinc oxide, the only realistic way to reprotect a fully made-up face at midday without ruining it. It blots shine at the same time, which suits combination and oily skin. Press it on with the puff rather than sweeping it, and take it to the hairline.

name: Second Skin Liquid Foundation
short: A medium-coverage liquid that dries down to skin and stays there.
description: Second Skin is a fluid foundation with buildable medium coverage that loses its finish entirely within two minutes and reads as skin by lunchtime. It moves with the face rather than cracking at the smile lines, and it photographs without a grey cast. Sixteen shades span cool, neutral and warm.
details: Dries down to a natural skin finish
Sixteen shades, cool neutral and warm
Shake before use, one pump is a full face

name: Serum Foundation Medium Coverage
short: Half skincare, half foundation, with hyaluronic acid and squalane inside.
description: A fluid foundation carrying hyaluronic acid, squalane and niacinamide so it behaves on skin that is drier than it was in September. The coverage is medium and melts in with a fingertip, never with a brush pressed hard. It wears best on skin prepped with nothing but a light moisturiser.
details: Medium coverage with a dewy-satin finish
Hyaluronic acid, squalane and niacinamide inside
Comfortable on dry and mature skin

name: Matte Velvet Foundation
short: A soft matte that powders on the skin instead of drying on it.
description: A matte foundation built with silica microspheres rather than alcohol, so it sets to velvet without the tight, papery feeling most longwear mattes leave behind. It holds through heat and through a full day under a mask. Use a thin layer and build only where you need it.

name: Bare Skin Tint
short: A sheer tint for the days when the only job is looking rested.
description: A watery tint with barely any pigment and a good deal of glycerin, made to even the colour of a face without anyone noticing a product on it. It will not hide anything and is not trying to. Ten shades, all of them translucent enough to be forgiving.

name: Cream Concealer Pot
short: A pot of full-coverage cream that does not crease when it is warm.
description: A dense, high-pigment cream concealer that needs warming on the lid of the pot before it will spread, which is exactly why it stays put. It covers marks, veins and tattoo edges with a small amount pressed rather than swiped. Twelve shades, from fair to deep.
details: Warm it on the lid before use
Twelve shades with a fine milled pigment

name: Brightening Under-Eye Concealer
short: A light-reflecting concealer for hollows, with caffeine in the base.
description: A fine, hydrating concealer with light-reflecting mica and a little caffeine, formulated thin enough not to settle into under-eye creases by four in the afternoon. It lifts shadow and hollowness rather than painting over it. One tiny dot, tapped out with a ring finger.
details: Hydrating base for the delicate eye area
Six shades tuned to neutralise blue and brown

name: Blur Primer
short: A silicone-soft primer that fills pores and gives foundation something to hold.
description: A smoothing, pore-filling primer with dimethicone and bamboo powder that turns textured skin into a level surface before any colour touches it. It works best pressed into the nose and cheeks alone, not the whole face. Foundation applied over it slides less and lasts longer.

name: Glow Primer
short: A luminous primer for skin that wants to look lit from the front.
description: A hydrating primer with fine light-catching pigments and squalane, for skin that goes flat under foundation in winter. It gives a soft sheen across the high points and stops powder from reading chalky. Use it alone with a concealer on the no-makeup days.

name: Pore Smoothing Primer
short: A mattifying primer with niacinamide for skin that slips by noon.
description: A weightless mattifying primer with niacinamide and zinc that keeps the shine down in the middle of the face and gives foundation a surface to sit on. It dries to a soft blur in about thirty seconds, so work in sections on hot days. A pea-size is the whole face.
details: Mattifying with niacinamide and zinc PCA
Dries to a soft blur in thirty seconds

name: Longwear Setting Spray
short: A fine mist that locks base makeup without the squeaky film.
description: A fast-drying setting spray with a flexible film-former that keeps foundation and concealer exactly where you put them through a long day and a warm room. It mist finely, dries in seconds and never leaves the face feeling lacquered. Hold it at arm length and cross the face twice.

name: Dewy Finish Setting Spray
short: A setting spray that puts the glow back after powder.
description: A hydrating mist that melts powder and foundation back into one surface and returns a dewy finish to a face that went flat at the compact stage. Panthenol and rice water sit in the base, so it is also a decent midday refresh. Two passes, held at arm length.

name: Loose Finishing Powder
short: A finely milled translucent powder that disappears instead of drying.
description: A silky, finely milled loose powder with silica and a small amount of squalane, which means it sets the face without pulling moisture out of it. It photographs without flashback and works on every depth of skin. Press it in with a sponge, then brush the excess away.
details: Four tints from translucent to deep
Press with a sponge, brush off excess

name: Pressed Setting Powder
short: The loose powder, pressed into a mirror case worth opening in public.
description: A pressed version of the same finely milled silica base, dense enough to travel and matte enough to blot a nose at a dinner table. The compact carries a real mirror and a velvet puff rather than a plastic scoop. Press, do not sweep, and it will not disturb the base under it.
details: Travel compact with a genuine mirror

name: Blurring Multipurpose Balm
short: One stick that evens the face, hides a shadow and softens a lip line.
description: A soft, blendable stick balm that evens tone across the whole face, works as an under-eye corrector when applied thin and conditions the lip line when applied thick. It is the product to keep in a bag, a desk drawer and a coat pocket. Six shades, all buildable to nothing.
details: Face, eye and lip in one stick

name: Cream Blush Pot
short: A pot of sheer cream pigment that reads like skin you have just walked in from the cold.
description: A whipped cream blush with a low pigment load, so you can build from nothing to a real flush in three taps without ever looking painted. It melts into bare skin and holds its colour through the evening. Dab it onto the apples with fingertips warm from rubbing them.

name: Liquid Blush Droplet
short: Three drops of pigment for a flush that comes from underneath.
description: A watery liquid blush that disperses evenly across the cheeks in seconds and dries to a finish indistinguishable from skin. Two or three drops on the back of the hand, then press on with a sponge or fingers. It layers over foundation without lifting it.
details: Press on with sponge or fingers

name: Powder Blush
short: A satin powder blush that goes on visible and dries down soft.
description: A finely milled powder blush with a satin finish, so it is easy to place accurately and hard to overdo. The pigment is honest on application and settles a shade softer within a minute. Sweep a fluffy brush along the cheekbone and blend upward toward the temple.
details: Ten shades across cool and warm

name: Cheek and Lip Balm
short: A tinted balm for both, in a tube that fits a jacket pocket.
description: A cushioned tinted balm that gives the cheeks a wash of colour and the lips a matching softness, with shea and jojoba underneath so neither goes dry. It wears off evenly instead of leaving a ring. Reapply from a mirror if you like; nobody will notice if you do not.
details: Two-use tint for cheeks and lips
Pocket tube with a sponge applicator

name: Terracotta Bronzer
short: A matte warm powder that reads as an afternoon, not as orange.
description: A baked terracotta bronzer with no shimmer and no orange in the pigment, made to warm the face where the sun would naturally hit it. It is buildable in sheer layers, which is the only way bronzer ever looks convincing. Sweep it along the hairline, the nose and the cheekbone.
details: Works with a flat or a fluffy brush

name: Powder Highlighter
short: A champagne highlighter fine enough to wear before noon.
description: A pressed highlighter with extremely fine, skin-melting pearl rather than visible glitter, so it catches the light at an angle and disappears head-on. It sits beautifully on bare skin and over powder alike. One pass on the cheekbone is the whole trick.
details: Press on the high points only
Beautiful over powder or bare skin
Four tones from pearl to bronze

name: Highlighter Stick
short: A cream highlight you can apply without a brush or a mirror.
description: A cushioned stick highlighter with a soft, wet-look sheen that you swipe and tap in with a fingertip in about ten seconds. It moves over the contours of the cheekbone instead of drawing a line across them. Squalane keeps it from clinging to texture.
details: Wet-look sheen that taps out softly
Squalane base, will not cling to texture

name: Blush Duo Compact
short: Two shades in one case for the cheekbone and the apple.
description: A baked duo with one deeper contour shade and one soft flush, designed to be swept together for a cheek that looks three-dimensional rather than flat. The pan is thin enough to layer and the case is slim enough for a small bag. Blend them together or keep them separate.
details: Slim travel case with a mirror

name: Eyeshadow Mono
short: A single baked shade that works as shadow, liner and a soft wash.
description: A baked mono with a buttery, low-fallout payoff that can be applied with a fingertip as a wash, or with a damp brush as a definable liner. The pigments are milled fine enough to sit flat on the lid all day. Nine shades, matte and satin, all of them buildable.
details: Use dry as a wash, damp as a liner

name: Eyeshadow Quad
short: Four coordinated shades that make the decision for you.
description: A quad built around one depth, one flush and two neutrals, chosen so that any combination of them works on a tired face in ninety seconds. The mattes blend cleanly and the satin sits in the middle of the lid without migrating. A genuine travel palette.
details: Four coordinated matte and satin shades
No shimmer in the crease shades

name: Studio Eyeshadow Palette
short: Twelve pans of the working shades, from bone to charcoal.
description: A twelve-pan palette built for the way most people actually use shadow: nine mattes in wearable depths and three finishes for the middle of the lid. Every matte is milled for low fallout and blends with a clean brush alone. It is the one palette to keep on a desk.
details: Blend with a clean brush, no primer needed

name: Liquid Eyeliner Pen
short: A felt tip with a genuinely fine point and an honest black.
description: A liquid liner with a firm felt tip that starts every time, in a black dense enough to read at the back of a room and a flexible film that survives a full day without flaking off at the outer corner. Draw from the middle of the lid outward, not from the inner corner. It dries in twenty seconds.

name: Gel Eyeliner Pot
short: A pot liner that stays workable for a minute, then sets for twelve hours.
description: A cream gel liner in a small sealed pot that gives you a moment to place a line precisely before it sets to a water-resistant finish. It smudges deliberately as a smoked liner if you want that, and refuses to move if you do not. Pair it with an angled brush and keep the lid closed.
details: Workable for sixty seconds, then sets
Pot stays soft with the lid sealed

name: Kohl Eyeliner Pencil
short: A soft kohl for the waterline that never pulls the lid.
description: A cushioned kohl pencil with enough slip to line the waterline without dragging, and enough pigment to make the eye look denser rather than drawn. It sets softly within a minute, so the smudge is intentional rather than accidental. Twist up, no sharpener to lose.
details: Cushioned glide, no dragging on the lid

name: Lengthening Mascara
short: A thin brush and a light formula for lashes that look longer, not heavier.
description: A lengthening mascara with a narrow tapered brush and a flexible film that combs each lash individually and stretches it a shade. It does not add much volume, and that is the honest trade for zero clumping and no evening fallout. Two coats, rolled from the root rather than pumped.
details: Rolled from the root, never pumped
Removes with warm water and a cotton pad

name: Volume Mascara
short: A dense brush with real thickness in it, for lashes that show across a room.
description: A volumising mascara with a plush hourglass brush and a wax-light formula that builds thickness without turning the lashes into a single black bar. Two coats take it from daytime to evening; three work if you have the patience. It holds a curl on straight lashes, which is rare.
details: Holds a curl on straight lashes

name: Waterproof Mascara
short: The one for humid months, tears and long days by water.
description: A genuinely waterproof mascara that survives rain, swimming and a difficult film without running, and still comes off in one stroke with an oil-based cleanser. The brush is slim and the formula is drier, so work quickly and do not let coats sit. It is not for daily wear; lashes dry out.
details: Removes with an oil cleanser in one stroke
Slim brush for the lower lashes
Reserve for long and wet days

name: Lash Primer
short: A white base coat that makes any mascara do more.
description: A fibres-and-wax primer applied before mascara that coats each lash, gives the colour underneath something to cling to, and adds visible length without a second tube. It sets in thirty seconds, so move quickly. It works equally well on bare lashes for a daytime lift.
details: Apply before mascara, in one pass
Adds lift and length without weight
Also good alone for a daytime lash

name: Clear Brow Gel
short: A transparent gel that holds hairs up all day without going crunchy.
description: A flexible clear gel with a small, precise brush that grooms brows upward and keeps them there without flaking white into the hair. It holds fine, stubborn hairs through humidity and disappears entirely on the brow. Use it on dry hair, brushing against the growth first.
details: No white flake on dry hair
Small stepped brush for short hairs

name: Tinted Brow Gel
short: Hold plus a soft wash of pigment for brows that are sparse at the tail.
description: A tinted gel that fills the look of a thin tail while keeping the hairs brushed up, with fibres fine enough not to read as a drawn line. Six tones cover most natural brow depths without going warm or orange. Apply thinly and comb through before it dries.
details: Tint and hold in one step

name: Microfine Brow Pencil
short: A 1.5 mm tip for hair strokes, not for blocks of colour.
description: An ultra-fine brow pencil that draws individual hair strokes at the tail and gaps between hairs, then softens with a spoolie before anyone can tell. The core is firm enough not to snap under a light hand and matte on the skin. Choose a shade lighter than you think.
details: 1.5 mm microfine tip for hair strokes

name: Brow Pomade Pot
short: A longwear pomade for brows that need structure, not just colour.
description: A concentrated pomade in a small pot, high in pigment and waterproof once dry, that lets you draw a crisp bottom edge and a soft top. A thin layer with an angled brush is the difference between groomed and severe. It is also the one that survives a beach holiday.

name: Brow Setting Wax
short: A matte wax for the days you want brows brushed flat and unbothered.
description: A medium-hold matte wax that laminates brow hairs in place without shine or stiffness, the kind of finish you used to need a professional to get. The wand is short and stubby so it coats the roots rather than the tips. Apply on dry hair, then press down with a fingertip.
details: Layer over powder for extra grip

name: Satin Lipstick
short: A true-colour bullet with a satin glide and no ring of colour left behind.
description: A medium-pigment lipstick in a satin finish, made from a shea and jojoba base that glides rather than drags and wears off evenly instead of leaving a hard ring. One pass covers; a second deepens. It is the bullet to reach for when your lips have been over-exfoliated.

name: Matte Velvet Lipstick
short: A genuine matte that does not feel like paper on the lips.
description: A full-pigment matte bullet built with a soft-focus wax that keeps the finish flat and the feel comfortable for a good four hours. It blurs the lip line rather than outlining it, so feathering is rare. Blot once after the first pass and it will stay put through coffee.
details: Blurs the lip line against feathering
Four to five hours of wear

name: Liquid Lip Colour
short: A transfer-resistant liquid matte that stops being sticky in a minute.
description: A flexible liquid matte that goes on comfortable, sets within sixty seconds and survives a masked afternoon without transferring in a line to the inside of the fabric. It is not a mousse and will not shrink into the lip lines as it dries. Remove it with an oil cleanser, not a wipe.
details: Does not shrink into lip lines
Six to eight hours of wear

name: Lip Liner Pencil
short: A blurring liner you can shade inward and no one will know why.
description: A cushioned lip pencil with a matte finish that defines the edge without drawing a line, then blends inward to deepen the middle of the lip. It works over balm and under lipstick equally well. Ten shades built to sit between real lip colours, not on top of them.
details: Layerable over balm and under colour

name: Sheer Lip Gloss
short: A non-sticky gloss with a real tint and none of the drag.
description: A cushioned gloss in a flat wide applicator, made with jojoba and squalane so it sits on the lip rather than pulling at it when you talk. It has enough colour to be a lip product on its own and enough shine to layer over any bullet. It does not migrate into lines.
details: Wear alone or over a bullet
Will not migrate into lip lines

name: Velvet Lip Ink
short: A stain-thin pigment that leaves colour behind even after the gloss goes.
description: A watery, deeply pigmented lip ink that sinks into the surface of the lip and stays as a soft stain for hours after the top layer has worn off. Apply it thin and let it dry before anything else touches it. It is the closest thing to a lip that looks naturally coloured.
details: Apply thin and let it dry

name: Cushion Lip Tint
short: A sponge-topped tint for the inside of the lip, blurred outward.
description: A soft blurring tint with a cushion applicator that presses colour into the centre of the lip and fades as it moves outward, which is how a natural flush actually behaves. It is lightly hydrating and completely sheer. Build in two passes rather than one heavy one.

name: Cream Lip Colour
short: A one-pass cream bullet in twelve shades you can wear as a blush too.
description: A soft cream lipstick with medium coverage that applies in a single pass and can be tapped onto the cheeks when you are in a hurry. The finish is a low shine, the kind that photographs well on dry lips. It is the most forgiving formula in the range.
details: Comfortable on dry or flaky lips

name: Longwear Lip Stain
short: A ten-hour stain in a flat shade, for days you will not see a mirror again.
description: A two-step stain with a pigment layer and a sealing balm layer that leaves a flat wash of colour behind long after the top has worn. It cannot be applied lazily; the edges matter. Once it has stained, eating changes very little about it.
details: Two steps, pigment then sealing balm
Flat colour, no shine once set
Apply precisely, it does not move later

name: Nail Lacquer
short: A one-coat colour with a flattop brush and a week of wear.
description: A chip-resistant lacquer with a wide flattop brush that covers most nails in two strokes per side and dries to a hard gloss within ten minutes. The pigment load is high enough that one pass reads as a colour, not as a suggestion. It comes off with acetone and a cotton pad, no peeling.
details: Two-stroke coverage with a wide brush
Dries hard and glossy in ten minutes
Chip-resistant for up to seven days

name: Strengthening Base Coat
short: A protein base coat that stops the bending before the chipping starts.
description: A hardening base coat with keratin-derived protein and calcium that gives a soft nail something to push against, and gives colour a surface to hold. Worn alone it leaves a faint milky gloss. Use it under every lacquer and on bare nails between manicures.
details: Wears alone as a milky gloss

specs.v: Base coat, alone or under colour

name: High Gloss Top Coat
short: A quick-dry top that keeps the shine past day four.
description: A fast-setting top coat that hardens the lacquer beneath it, adds real depth of shine and stops the tips wearing through by Thursday. Swipe a little along the free edge as well and it will hold the colour in. It does not thicken or go stringy in the bottle.
details: Deep gloss that outlasts the colour
Seal the free edge for fewer chips

name: Cuticle and Nail Oil
short: A pen of fractionated coconut and jojoba for the skin around the nail.
description: A brush-tipped oil pen with fractionated coconut oil, jojoba and vitamin E that sinks into the cuticle without leaving your hands slippery an hour later. It keeps the ridge and hangnail look away between manicures. Carry one and use it while reading, not only after polish.

specs.v: Jojoba, fractionated coconut oil, vitamin E

name: Daily Cream Shampoo
short: A sulphate-free cream wash for hair that gets dry at the ends.
description: A gentle, sulphate-free cream shampoo that cleans the scalp without squeezing the lengths dry, built on a mild surfactant blend with panthenol. It barely lathers, which takes about a week to get used to. Use it on the scalp only and let the suds run down on the rinse.
details: Panthenol and glycerin in the base

name: Clarifying Reset Shampoo
short: A clear wash with charcoal for the week of dry shampoo and hard water.
description: A clarifying shampoo with activated charcoal and a chelating agent that lifts mineral build-up, silicones and the residue of a long dry-shampoo streak. It is not a daily habit; use it once a fortnight and follow with a mask. Hair squeaks clean in the good sense, not the straw sense.
details: Activated charcoal with a chelating agent
Once every one to two weeks
Follow with a conditioner or mask

name: Scalp Renewal Shampoo
short: Zinc and salicylic acid for a scalp that flakes and itches in winter.
description: A cleansing shampoo with zinc PCA and 2 per cent salicylic acid that helps clear the look of flakes and settles the itch of a tight, reactive scalp. Leave it on for a minute before rinsing, then condition the lengths only. Use it three times a week through the cold months.
details: Zinc PCA with 2 per cent salicylic acid
Helps clear the look of flakes
Hold for sixty seconds before rinsing

name: Volumising Rice Protein Shampoo
short: A light wash with rice protein that lifts fine hair off the head.
description: A weightless shampoo fortified with hydrolysed rice protein, which temporarily thickens the individual strand so fine hair holds shape at the crown. It cleans thoroughly and leaves nothing coating the hair. Alternate with a moisture shampoo, since protein every day goes stiff.
details: Lifts the crown within one wash

name: Colour Care Shampoo
short: A gentle, slightly acidic wash that keeps a colour from running.
description: A colour-safe shampoo formulated at a low pH with camellia oil and green tea, so the cuticle stays closed and the pigment stays inside it. It is mild enough for daily use on bleached hair. Wash the scalp and let the ends be cleaned by nothing but the runoff.
details: Safe on bleached and fashion colour

name: Oat Comfort Shampoo
short: A milk-soft wash for a scalp that burns after every other shampoo.
description: A milky, ultra-mild shampoo with colloidal oatmeal and squalane for scalps that go hot and tight under ordinary surfactants. It cleans lightly and honestly, which is often all a dry scalp needs. Skip it on the days you use the renewal shampoo.

name: Caffeine Density Shampoo
short: A stimulating wash with caffeine and niacinamide for a thinning look.
description: A daily shampoo with caffeine, niacinamide and rice peptide that supports the look of denser, fuller hair at the crown by keeping the scalp itself clean and unhindered. It will not regrow anything, and we would rather say that than promise it. Massage for a minute, then rinse.
details: Caffeine with niacinamide and rice peptide
Supports the look of fuller hair

name: Curl Cleansing Co-Wash
short: A conditioning wash for curls that cannot survive shampoo twice a week.
description: A co-wash that lifts dust and light oil from curly hair without the foam that leaves it frizzy and expanded. It is formulated to rinse fully, which ordinary conditioner never quite does. Use it between shampoos, on the mid-lengths and ends, and always on soaking wet hair.
details: For coily, curly and wavy hair

name: Post-Workout Scalp Shampoo
short: A light clarifying wash for the gym bag and the sweat on the scalp.
description: A low-foam gel shampoo with willow bark extract and mint that takes sweat, salt and odour off the scalp after a session without drying out the lengths. The bottle is small enough to live in a gym kit permanently. Rinse once, wash, rinse again, and be out of the shower in three minutes.
details: Willow bark with a touch of mint

name: Bond Care Strengthening Shampoo
short: A protein-light wash for hair that snaps at the mid-lengths.
description: A strengthening shampoo with a peptide complex and a small amount of hydrolysed protein, built for hair that has been heat-styled and bleached into brittleness. It supports the look of fewer breakages over six weeks, which is a slow and honest claim. Follow with the bond masque once a week.
details: Reduces the look of breakage over weeks

name: Daily Moisture Conditioner
short: A mid-weight cream that detangles without making hair lie flat.
description: A everyday conditioner with cetyl alcohol, glycerin and a little squalane that gives slip where it is needed and rinses out clean. It is the one to hand to whoever keeps borrowing your products. Apply from the ears down, leave two minutes, rinse cool.
details: Apply from the ears down only

name: Slip Detangling Conditioner
short: Serious slip for knots, kids and anyone with a wide-tooth comb.
description: A thick, high-slip conditioner that turns a brushing session from a negotiation into a ninety-second job. It works on damp hair with a wide-tooth comb, starting at the ends and working upward. It is heavy, so keep it well away from the roots.
details: Also good on wet tangles after swimming

name: Weightless Conditioner for Fine Hair
short: A watery conditioner that does the job and then leaves.
description: A thin, water-based conditioner with hydrolysed rice protein and panthenol, made for hair that goes flat under anything creamier. It detangles lightly and rinses out with no film at all. A hazelnut amount on the ends is the entire dose.
details: Will not weigh fine hair down
Layer under a leave-in if needed

name: Curl Defining Conditioner
short: A rich rinse that leaves curls clumped, shaped and not frizzed.
description: A conditioning cream with shea and camellia oil that encourages curls to form into proper clumps rather than a cloud. Detangle it in with fingers under running water, then rinse partly, leaving a little behind. It is the base of a good wash day for textured hair.

name: Colour Shield Conditioner
short: A slightly acidic conditioner that keeps dye from leaching out.
description: A low-pH conditioner with green tea and camellia that keeps the cuticle closed after a salon visit and slows the fade of fashion shades. It slips well enough for bleached hair without softening it into mush. Use it on every wash for the first month after colouring.
details: pH 4.5 to hold the cuticle closed
Daily through the first month after colour

name: Keratin Repair Conditioner
short: A protein conditioner for hair that stretches when it is wet.
description: A conditioner with hydrolysed keratin and amino acids that temporarily fills in the porous patches of over-processed hair, so it stops going limp and elastic when wet. Use it in cycles, two weeks on and two off, because too much protein makes hair brittle rather than strong. Follow with moisture on the other washes.
details: For hair that stretches when wet
Cycle two weeks on, two off
Follow with a moisture conditioner between
Focus on the most damaged lengths

name: Argan and Camellia Hair Oil
short: Two cold-pressed oils, one pump, and no grease on the pillow.
description: A blend of argan and camellia oils light enough to use on damp hair before drying and on dry ends mid-afternoon. One pump warmed between the palms takes the frizz down without making the hair look unwashed. It has no silicone in it, which is why it needs reapplying rather than building up.
details: One pump on damp or dry ends
Safe before heat styling at low heat

name: Scalp Oil, Vetiver and Cedar
short: A pre-wash scalp oil with vetiver for dryness and a slow evening scent.
description: A light pre-wash oil of fractionated coconut, jojoba and a real vetiver and cedar distillate that loosens flaky buildup on a Sunday night and smells like a good library. Massage a dropper into the partings, leave an hour, then shampoo twice. It is not a leave-in; the scalp will tell you.
details: Pre-wash treatment, one to two hours

name: Lightweight Shine Oil
short: A dry oil in a spray for fine hair that cannot carry weight.
description: A mist of fractionated coconut oil and a small amount of camellia that gives fine hair a surface shine and a little slip without a single visible drop of grease. Spray it onto the palms, then run them over the mid-lengths. It is also the right oil for the days you wore too much of the rich one.
details: Apply to palms, then to lengths

name: Overnight Ritual Oil
short: A heavier pressing of marula and rice bran for very dry, coarse hair.
description: Marula, rice bran and a little castor oil in an overnight treatment oil for coarse, high-porosity hair that drinks everything it is given. Warm a teaspoon, work it through the lengths, braid loosely and wash it out in the morning. It softens the look of roughness from the first week.
details: Overnight treatment, rinse out in the morning
Marula, rice bran and castor oils
Braid loosely to keep it off the pillow
For coarse and very dry hair

name: Hair Mist, Neroli and Bergamot
short: A scent for the hair that does not contain the alcohol of a perfume.
description: A light fragrance mist with neroli and bergamot in a glycerin-and-water base, made to sit on the hair rather than the skin, where alcohol would be a problem. It holds for a few hours and takes the shape of whatever perfume you are wearing underneath. Spray the brush, not the head.
details: Spray onto a brush and comb through

name: Shea and Marula Hair Masque
short: A ten-minute masque that turns a straw-like feel back into hair.
description: A dense masque with shea butter, marula oil and cetyl alcohol that softens dry, rough lengths in about ten minutes under warm water. Use it weekly on the mid-lengths and ends, never the scalp. It is thick enough that a wide-tooth comb does the distributing for you.
details: Rinse with warm, then cool water

name: Keratin Smooth Mask
short: A protein mask for the weeks between straightening services.
description: A smoothing masque with hydrolysed keratin and amino acids that temporarily flattens the surface of porous hair, so it dries straighter and frizzes less in humidity. Fifteen minutes with a shower cap, then a thorough rinse. Alternate it with a moisture masque; protein alone will make hair snap.

name: Clay Scalp Purifying Mask
short: A kaolin scalp paste for the week the roots go flat by Tuesday.
description: A cooling kaolin and zinc mask that you paint onto the partings, leave for ten minutes and rinse out before it dries into a mess. It lifts oil and product buildup from the scalp and leaves the roots visibly lighter. Keep it away from the lengths, which it will only dry.
details: Apply to the partings on dry hair
Ten minutes, rinse before it hardens
Use every one to two weeks

name: Bond Repair Masque
short: The weekly intensive for hair that has been through too much bleach.
description: A peptide-and-protein masque formulated to support the look of strength in hair that has been lightened repeatedly, with a conditioning base so it never goes stiff. Twenty minutes on damp lengths, then rinse. It cannot rebuild what has been removed, but it does make the last two inches survivable.

name: Leave-In Cream
short: A light everyday cream for damp hair, comb-through soft.
description: A milky leave-in with panthenol, glycerin and a small amount of cetyl alcohol that keeps damp hair manageable until it dries and then does nothing visible. It is the right first product for anyone who has never used one. A coin-size for shoulder-length hair, more for more.

name: Detangling Mist
short: A spray for dry hair, knots and the eight in the morning brushing session.
description: A watery mist with a small amount of conditioning agent that gives dry, knotted hair enough slip to comb through without pulling chunks out. It dries weightless, so it works on second-day hair as well as wet. Spray, wait thirty seconds, then comb from the ends upward.
details: Spray on dry or damp hair

name: Heat Protectant Cream
short: A blow-dry cream that shields up to 200 degrees and speeds the dry.
description: A styling cream with a heat-shielding polymer and squalane that cuts blow-drying time noticeably and keeps the straightening iron from grabbing. It is comfortable on damp hair and never flakes once dry. Use it every single time you apply heat, without exception.
details: Protects up to 200 C styling heat

name: Curl Defining Cream
short: A shaping cream that keeps the pattern and leaves the crunch out.
description: A defining cream with shea and a light hold that encourages curl clumps, dries soft and refuses to leave a cast unless you scrunch it out. Apply it soaking wet, in sections, raking then scrunching. On wavy hair, use half the amount you think you need.
details: Apply to soaking wet hair in sections

name: Anti-Frizz Hair Serum
short: A silicone-smooth serum that stops humidity winning the argument.
description: A concentrated serum with cyclomethicone and argan oil that flattens the frizz halo on damp or dry hair and holds it through a humid day. Two drops is a full head; more simply makes the lengths look flat and oily. It sits on the surface and washes out with a clarifying shampoo.
details: Two drops for the whole head
Keep well away from the roots

name: Sea Salt Texture Spray
short: Grit and volume for hair that dries too polite.
description: A light salt-and-sugar spray with a little algae extract that gives straight or wavy hair the piece-y texture of a day spent near water. Scrunch it into damp hair or refresh dry lengths with a mist. It will dry out very porous hair if used daily, so alternate days.
details: Scrunch into damp or mist onto dry

name: Rice Starch Dry Shampoo
short: A translucent rice powder that absorbs oil and leaves no white head.
description: A dry shampoo milled from rice starch rather than the usual aerosol powders, so it absorbs oil at the root and blends to nothing on dark hair. It comes in a pump, which means no propellant and no cloud in a small bathroom. Two sprays per section, then massage it in.

name: Flexible Hold Styling Gel
short: A gel that holds a shape and then lets you move your head.
description: A water-based gel with a flexible film that keeps a fringe down or a parting crisp without going glassy, and washes out in a single rinse. It works on dry hair for edge control and on damp hair for shape. Use a pea-size, not the handful the tube encourages.
details: Works on damp or dry hair

name: Glossing Shine Spray
short: A fine mist for hair that looks matte under office lighting.
description: A light spray of fractionated coconut oil and a hydrolysed protein that puts a real reflection back on dull lengths for a day and then washes away. Mist it at a distance onto dry hair and comb once through. It is a cosmetic shine, not a treatment, and it is honest about it.
details: Also good on the ends after styling

name: Scalp Serum with Peptide and Caffeine
short: A dropper-to-the-parting serum for the look of a healthier scalp.
description: A lightweight leave-on serum with a peptide complex, caffeine and niacinamide that keeps the scalp comfortable and supports the look of denser-looking hair over three months of nightly use. The nozzle puts product onto the parting, not into the hair. It does not sting, and it does not smell medicinal.
details: Peptide complex with caffeine and niacinamide
Non-greasy, no residue in the hair
Patch test first, as with any active

name: Exfoliating Scalp Lotion
short: Salicylic acid in a runny lotion for buildup that shampoo will not shift.
description: A thin 2 per cent salicylic acid lotion applied to dry partings twice a week, which loosens the compacted oil and flakes ordinary washing leaves behind. Leave it overnight or for two hours, then shampoo out. Expect a little more shedding in the first fortnight, which is the buildup going.
details: Apply to dry partings twice weekly

name: Pre-Wash Scalp Treatment
short: An oil-and-clay paste that lifts buildup before the water runs.
description: A pre-wash paste of bentonite, squalane and willow bark that you work into the scalp on dry hair, leave for fifteen minutes and then shampoo away twice. It pulls compacted oil out of the follicle opening rather than scrubbing at it. Use it monthly, or fortnightly on very oily scalps.
details: Bentonite with squalane and willow bark
Monthly, or fortnightly if very oily
Do not apply to broken skin

name: Post-Wash Scalp Tonic
short: A cooling tonic of menthol and panthenol for the shower exit.
description: A watery leave-on tonic with a low level of menthol, panthenol and green tea that cools a hot, tight scalp straight out of the shower and dries without leaving the hair looking wet. It is fragrance-light and safe to use daily on the days you wash. Press it in with fingertips, do not soak the lengths.
details: Leave-on, applied to a clean scalp
Menthol with panthenol and green tea
Press in, do not soak the lengths

name: Hair UV Mist
short: Sunscreen for the hair, because colour does not survive a beach either.
description: A fine protective mist with a light UV filter and hydrolysed protein that shields the lengths on exposed days, the part of the hair routine almost nobody does. Mist it onto dry hair before going out and reapply after swimming. It leaves no stiffness and no scent worth mentioning.

name: Blonde Tone Shampoo
short: A violet-pigmented wash that keeps bleach from going brassy.
description: A toning shampoo with direct violet pigment that pulls the yellow out of bleached, grey and highlighted hair over three minutes. Two uses a week is plenty; more turns the ends lilac, which washes out but is not the plan. Condition the ends afterwards, because toning shampoos are drying.

name: Ivory Thread Eau de Parfum
short: Iris, ambrette and white musk, worn close enough to need leaning in.
description: Ivory Thread opens on powdered iris and cold musk and stays there, a skin scent with structure rather than a trail. Orris butter gives it a soft, slightly carrot-like depth that never goes sweet. It is the quietest bottle in the range and the one people ask about on the second day.
details: Iris pallida orris butter as the heart
Ambrette seed for a clean, cottony musk
Reads closer to skin in the first hour, then softens
Best layered over an unscented moisturiser

name: Vetiver Hour Eau de Parfum
short: Smoke, grapefruit peel and a root that is dry rather than earthy.
description: A Haiti-derived vetiver kept green and airy with grapefruit peel and a little cedar, so it reads like an outdoor evening rather than a barbershop. It gains a faint smudge of tobacco after an hour and holds that shape until the sixth. Strongly seasonal in autumn and winter.
details: Haitian vetiver root, dry and green
Grapefruit peel keeps the opening bright
A faint tobacco shadow after an hour
Projects for two hours, then sits closer
Spray on clothing for longer wear

name: Amber Ledger Eau de Parfum
short: Warm resin, labdanum and a low hum of vanilla that never turns gourmand.
description: A dry amber built on labdanum, benzoin and a trace of vanilla, weighted with immortelle so it stays resinous instead of dessert-like. It is warm in the way a room is warm after the fire has gone down. Excellent in cold weather and overpowering in a small lift.
details: Only a trace of vanilla, no sweetness

name: Skin Musk Eau de Toilette
short: A clean-skin scent: musk, a little aldehydic air, nothing else.
description: A short list of white musks with a soft aldehydic lift, made to smell like warm skin that has just been washed. It has no top note worth describing and does not pretend otherwise. Wear it under another perfume and it will make that perfume last longer.
details: Soft aldehydic opening, soapy not powdery

name: Neroli Dawn Eau de Toilette
short: Orange blossom taken seriously: green, honeyed and briefly bitter.
description: Tunisian neroli distillate with a green petitgrain edge and a small amount of honeyed orange flower absolute, so the citrus never collapses into soap. It is bright for twenty minutes and then turns soft and skin-adjacent. The only true daytime floral in the collection.
details: A trace of honeyed orange flower absolute
Fades sooner than the heavier flacons
Reapply from a travel size at midday

name: Bergamot Report Eau de Toilette
short: A cologne for people who like citrus, and then want it to last.
description: Calabrian bergamot with lemon peel, a mineral ambergris accord and a dry cedar tail, structured so the citrus survives the first hour instead of vanishing in it. It is the scent of a clean shirt in a warm room. Keep it refrigerated in summer and use it freely.
details: Ambroxan for a mineral, saline tail
Dry cedar keeps the base honest
A cologne that outlasts most colognes
Pleasant on skin and on cotton

name: Sandal Silence Eau de Parfum
short: Creamy sandalwood with saffron on top and almost nothing else.
description: Australian sandalwood in a soft, milky register, lifted with a thread of saffron and held by tonka. There is no smoke here and no leather; it is the smooth end of the wood family. It settles into a second skin by the third hour and stays there all day.
details: A thread of saffron for warmth

name: Jasmine Index Eau de Parfum
short: Night-blooming jasmine, green stem and a low note of musk.
description: A sambac jasmine built with its own green, slightly tea-like stem note intact, so the flower keeps its edge instead of going indolic and heavy. A whisper of bergamot opens it and a clean musk closes it. It reads as a real flower, not as a candle.
details: Jasmine sambac with green stem intact
Strongest in the first ninety minutes

name: Oud Interval Extrait de Parfum
short: A smoked, rose-led oud that behaves itself in warm weather.
description: A synthetic accord that captures the dry, woody side of oud, with a small dose of rose and a resinous amber behind it. It has no barnyard sting, which makes it wearable where real oud usually is not. Three applications only, and one of them should be on a scarf.
details: Oud accord, dry and smoked rather than animalic

name: Ember Saffron Eau de Parfum
short: Saffron and leather over amber, warm and slightly metallic.
description: A saffron-led opening with a faint metallic heat over soft leather and amber, built to be noticed without being loud. It behaves best in cool weather, where the resin stays pliable rather than cloying. Two sprays on the chest and one on the collar.
details: Saffron with a warm metallic edge
Two to three applications is the dose

name: Green Tea and Cedar Eau de Toilette
short: Steamed green tea, cedar needle and a saline top that reads cold.
description: A green, faintly bitter tea note over cedar needles and a mineral salt accord, made for people who find citrus too sharp and woods too heavy. It stays close to the skin and refreshes rather than announces. Good in the middle of a working day.

name: Fig Leaf Water Eau de Toilette
short: Green fig, milky coconut leaf and a wet-stone coolness.
description: A sapchy green fig leaf note with a thin coconut milk accord and a mineral base that makes the whole thing smell slightly damp, in the best sense. It is the most photogenic scent we make and one of the most wearable in heat. Reapply generously; it is light by design.
details: Green fig leaf with a milky coconut trace

name: Iso E Cloud Eau de Toilette
short: Iso E super, cedar and ambrette, sanded down to a halo.
description: A study in a single molecule: iso E super at a high dose with cedar and a musky ambrette underneath, velvety, translucent and hard to describe to anyone else. It seems to vanish and then reappear when someone stands close. A layering scent that makes other perfumes look warmer.
details: Superb over any other scent in the range

name: Ambroxan 07 Eau de Parfum
short: Ambergris mineral warmth, saline and clean as a struck match.
description: A high dose of ambroxan with a saline top and a dry woody base, which reads at once like skin, like the sea and like nothing that has ever been bottled. It projects surprisingly far and lasts a long time on fabric. Wear it alone, or over a citrus to give the citrus a spine.
details: Saline top with a dry woody base
Lasts days on scarves and collars
Pairs with every citrus in the range

name: Rose Ash Eau de Parfum
short: A damask rose pushed through woodsmoke and a little incense.
description: A real rose absolute held back by birch tar smoke and cool incense, so the flower never gets jammy or old-fashioned. It is the most dramatic scent in the collection and still an everyday one if you are careful with the trigger. Two sprays, on the collarbone, in cool weather.

name: Coffee Amber Extrait
short: Roasted coffee and amber, dark and savoury rather than sweet.
description: A coffee absolute with no sugar in sight, wrapped in amber and a trace of cardamom for lift. It is dense, slightly burnt and grown-up, closer to a dark roast at the bottom of a pot than to a dessert. Extremely concentrated; a single pass of the glass stopper is the dose.
details: Amber resin warmth with cardamom lift
Apply with the glass stopper, once
Lasts through a full working day

name: Iris Powder Extrait
short: Orris butter and tonka under a veil of fine violet powder.
description: Aged orris butter at the centre, with violet leaf, tonka and a soft suede note that makes the whole thing smell like a powder room with the window open. It is cool-toned and dry, and it improves enormously on skin that has been moisturised. Six-hour wear from one application.
details: Aged orris butter, cool and dry
Violet leaf for a green powder effect

name: Tuberose Archive Eau de Parfum
short: Tuberose at full volume, with a green stalk and no coconut.
description: A heady tuberose built with its own green stalk note so it keeps a spine, plus a small jasmine dose and a sandalwood floor underneath. It is the most opulent scent in the range and the least suitable for an office in July. Wear it to be remembered.
details: Sandalwood floor keeps it from flying apart

name: Cedar Salt Eau de Parfum
short: Needle, mineral salt and grey amber, cold and unhurried.
description: A cedar-heavy woody with a saline grey amber accord that pulls it in a cold, mineral direction, and a thread of vetiver underneath. It wears clean rather than warm and works in every season. The kind of scent people describe as tidy.
details: Grey amber for a saline mineral edge

name: Rain on Stone Eau de Toilette
short: Petrichor: wet slate, geosmin and a green mineral hush.
description: Built around geosmin, the compound that gives the first rain on dry ground its smell, with violet leaf and a cool mineral accord behind it. It is literal, quiet and slightly uncanny, and it disappears sooner than the heavier flacons. Spray on the forearms so you can keep checking.
details: Geosmin at a low, convincing dose

name: Chamomile Ink Eau de Toilette
short: Blue chamomile, hay and warm rice, calm in a bottle.
description: Roman chamomile with its apple-sweet blue oil intact, laid over dry hay, tonka and a note of steamed rice that keeps it savoury. It is the most soothing scent in the range and reads as quiet rather than herbal medicine. Lovely on a pillow spray, less so in a boardroom.
details: Also good as a linen mist

name: Vanilla Bark Eau de Parfum
short: Vanilla used as a wood, with benzoin and black pepper.
description: A raw, unsweetened vanilla absolute treated like a resin, with benzoin, black pepper and a cedar underneath, so the result is smoky and dry rather than bakery-sweet. It is the vanilla for people who say they dislike vanilla. Long wear and gentle sillage at the same time.
details: Benzoin resin for a smoky dryness
Black pepper keeps the top awake

name: Lavender Vetiver Eau de Toilette
short: High-altitude lavender over a green vetiver, fougere without the soap.
description: A fresh lavender with a herbal, slightly camphorous top, sitting on a green vetiver and coumarin rather than the usual tonka-and-soap structure. It reads as classic and modern at once and behaves well in heat. Good on damp skin straight out of the shower.
details: Green vetiver instead of a powdery base
Apply to damp skin for even wear

name: Black Tea Absolute Eau de Parfum
short: Steeped black tea, bergamot peel and a note of smoke at the rim.
description: A dried tea leaf absolute with a little bergamot and a whisper of lapsang smoke, bitter-ish, warm and faintly tannic in the way a good cup is. It wears closer than its concentration suggests and suits grey weather and wool. It is also, quietly, the best seller in the range.
details: Black tea absolute, tannic and warm
Bergamot peel for a bitter top

name: Leather Margin Eau de Parfum
short: Suede-textured leather with saffron and dry birch, quiet and matte.
description: A soft, matte leather built with an isobutyl quinoline note kept at a low level, plus saffron and cedar, so it reads as a well-worn book cover rather than a new car interior. It is unisex in the plainest sense and improves with age in the bottle. Three sprays maximum.
details: Cedar and a low-level quinoline note
Improves with six months in the bottle

name: Petitgrain Light Eau de Toilette
short: Bitter orange leaf, sparkling and short, for the hottest months.
description: A petitgrain-and-mandarin opening with a dry wood base that keeps it from becoming a cologne for teenagers. It evaporates honestly within four hours, which is the correct behaviour for a citrus in August. Keep the bottle in the fridge and use it after shaving.
details: Ideal for high heat and post-shave

name: White Amber Eau de Toilette
short: A clean amber: musk, light wood and almost no resin.
description: The amber structure stripped of its heaviness, leaving a soft musky warmth with cedar and a mineral note, so it reads warm without ever reading sweet. This is the safest first bottle for someone who does not know what they like. It layers well beneath any of the florals.
details: White musk for a warm floor
Cedar and mineral salt on top

name: Amber Roll-On Perfume Oil
short: The amber formula, in a fractionated coconut base, at twelve per cent.
description: A roll-on oil version of the amber accord, diluted in fractionated coconut oil with vitamin E, which means no alcohol and no spray cloud in a shared room. It stays close to the skin for four or five hours and is easy to reapply at a desk. Good for people whose skin finds alcohol drying.
details: Close wear, easy to top up

name: Discovery Trio
short: Three 5 ml sprays of the range, in a cotton pouch you might keep.
description: Ivory Thread, Vetiver Hour and Ambroxan 07 in refillable 5 ml sprays, which is the only reasonable way to find out which of the three you actually want to live in. The atomisers are real, not the sample bulbs that fail after two uses. Return the pouch and we refill the sprays at a discount.
details: Atomisers tested for two hundred uses

name: Neroli Body Mist
short: A light, low-alcohol mist for the body that smells like an orange grove.
